long_biography.plain_text:
Menin studied civil engineering at the Federal University of Minas Gerais and trained at Vega Engenharia. Before MRV, he built an early house with a cousin using a family loan. In 1979, he joined Mário Menin, Homero Paiva and Vega to establish the company around lower-cost homes, then scaled that model across Brazil.

He led MRV as chief executive for decades before moving to the board chair in 2014. The group added LOG Commercial Properties, Urba and a United States multifamily business, while Menin separately founded Banco Inter and backed news broadcasting, radio and wine ventures. His children now hold senior positions in MRV and Inter, within governance structures that Menin began professionalising before MRV's public listing.
